title: Run your first program
subtitle: A program is a sequence of instructions. Start by displaying two lines in order.
concept: A program is a sequence of instructions. Start by displaying two lines in order.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Run your first program A program is a sequence of instructions. Start by displaying two lines in order. Think of a checklist: do the first item, then the second. Display one message Read print("Hello") as ‘display Hello’. Python provides print to display values. Parentheses hold the content, and matching straight quotes mark it as text. The quotes themselves are not printed. Try the example before memorizing terminology. Save two lines as a program Use the web demonstration to inspect execution order. To run the example on your computer, follow the four setup steps below and save both lines in hello.py. After changing code, save before running it again. Change one message at a time Python reads these lines from top to bottom: the first displays Hello; the second displays I am learning Python. Change only the second message and run again: the first should stay the same. A comment starts with # and is skipped during execution. Use straight quotes and ordinary code punctuation. print(...) displays its contents. These statements execute from top to bottom. Display two messages and check their order. Display two things you want to do today. Predict the output of print("Good morning"). Display First step, then Second step. Change the greeting to Hello, Lin. A comment is followed by print("Done"). How many lines are displayed?

title: Give values names
subtitle: Name a value so the next line can find it.
concept: Name a value so the next line can find it.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Give values names Name a value so the next line can find it. Attach an apple-count label to a basket holding 3 apples. Name a number apples = 3 associates the name apples with the number 3. Assignment evaluates the right side first, then updates the name on the left. print(apples) reads that value; print("apples") instead displays the literal word. Updating a name replaces its value In apples = apples + 2, the right side reads the old value 3 and adds 2 to obtain 5. Assignment then makes apples refer to 5. This is an instruction, not a mathematical equation that must hold forever. Follow the variable cards one line at a time. Numbers and text serve different purposes 3 is a number for arithmetic; "3" is text. Use a number for a count and text for a name. Names are case-sensitive: apples and Apples differ. This book uses lowercase English names and underscores between words, such as apple_count. Assignment evaluates the right side before updating the left-hand name. A quoted name is literal text. Start with 3 apples, add 2, and display the new total. Compare apples with and without quotes. After count = 4, what does print(count) display? Increase count from 4 to 5. Assign the text Lin to name, then display it. After a = 2; b = a; a = 5, what is b?

title: Numbers and arithmetic
subtitle: For the same candies, you can ask for an average or for full bags and leftovers.
concept: For the same candies, you can ask for an average or for full bags and leftovers.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Numbers and arithmetic For the same candies, you can ask for an average or for full bags and leftovers. 17 candies packed 5 per bag fill 3 bags, with 2 left over. Use familiar arithmetic Python uses + for addition, - for subtraction, * for multiplication, and / for division. For example, 3 * 5 gives 15 and 17 / 5 gives 3.4. Do not quote numbers. print(3 * 5) calculates before displaying. Multiplication and division precede addition and subtraction; use parentheses to change the order, as in (2 + 3) * 4. Find full bags and leftovers For full bags only, 17 // 5 gives 3. The two slashes perform floor division. For these nonnegative quantities, this is the full-bag count. 17 % 5 gives the remainder 2; here % does not mean percent. Three bags use 15 candies, leaving 17 - 15 = 2. Reconstruct the original total Multiply full bags by capacity and add leftovers: 3 * 5 + 2 = 17. If 20 candies fit 5 per bag, the remainder is 0. Change the total, then the capacity, one at a time. Counts are nonnegative integers and bag capacity must be positive. For this nonnegative-integer packing model, // gives full bags and % gives leftovers: bags times capacity plus remainder equals total. With capacity 5, display full bags and leftovers. How many candies remain after packing 20 with capacity 5? How many candies are in 3 bags with 5 per bag? Pack 12 candies with capacity 5. Find full bags and leftovers. Add 3 candies to an initial 17, then pack with capacity 5. Find the remainder. With only 3 candies and capacity 5, can you fill a bag?

title: Read text and quantities
subtitle: input receives text. Convert it to a number before doing arithmetic.
concept: input receives text. Convert it to a number before doing arithmetic.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Read text and quantities input receives text. Convert it to a number before doing arithmetic. Typing 3 first supplies the character 3; conversion makes it a quantity. Read one line from the user name = input() waits for a line. Pressing Enter delivers the text to name, without the final newline. You can first display print("What is your name?") to explain what to enter. Text values are called strings. Convert a quantity from text to a number Read count = int(input()) in two stages: input() receives text, then int(...) converts integer text such as "3" to the number 3. Now count + 2 can increase a quantity. Text such as "three" or "3.5" fails this integer conversion. Lesson 4.4 explains how to handle such errors. Insert variables into a message In print(f"Hello, {name}"), f marks a string whose brace fields are filled with values. {name} is replaced by the variable's value. This basic form is enough for now. To display a count by itself, print(count) also works. input() reads a string; int(...) converts valid integer text to a number; an f-string inserts values using {variable_name}. Enter Lin and display a greeting. Enter 3 and display the quantity after adding 2. Enter Wang and display the name unchanged. Enter 4 and display twice its value. Enter Lin and display Welcome, Lin. Enter 0, then add 2. What is the result?

title: Conditions and branches
subtitle: Test a condition, then take one of two paths.
concept: Test a condition, then take one of two paths.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Conditions and branches Test a condition, then take one of two paths. If you have enough money for the fare, take the bus. Otherwise, take the other path. Turn a question into a condition Suppose the fare is 5 and money holds the amount you have. money >= 5 asks whether you have at least 5; >= means greater than or equal to. A comparison returns True or False. Predict the result before following the program. Write two paths with if and else if condition: starts the path taken when the condition is true; else: starts the other path. After each colon, start a new line and indent the body by four spaces. Indentation groups statements into a branch. This test takes one branch: it cannot print both messages. Check the exact boundary Try 6, then 4, then exactly 5. The >= comparison includes equality, so 5 is enough. Replacing it with > would reject the exact fare. Use == to compare equality; a single = assigns a value. An if statement runs its indented body when the condition is true. Otherwise it runs the else body. Only one branch runs. You have 5 and the fare is 5. Display the decision. Test the same condition with 4. Predict the value of 6 >= 5. With 3, display Not enough money. Display Pass for a score of at least 60 and Practice again otherwise. Test 60. Test the same program with 59.

title: for loops and counting
subtitle: A for loop repeats an operation with a new value each time.
concept: A for loop repeats an operation with a new value each time.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python for loops and counting A for loop repeats an operation with a new value each time. Call numbers 1, 2, and 3 without writing the same instruction three times. Print a sequence of numbers for number in range(1, 4): gives number the values 1, 2, and 3 in turn. range produces integers: it includes 1 but excludes 4. The indented print(number) runs once per value, producing three lines. Set stop one beyond the last number To count through 5, write range(1, 6). With one argument, range(3) starts at 0 and produces 0, 1, 2. Here we use an explicit start and stop. After the loop, execution continues with the next unindented statement. Build a running total To add 1 + 2 + 3, start with total = 0 and add each number. The running total changes from 0 to 1 to 3 to 6. Place print(total) outside the loop to print only the final total. A for loop repeats over items. range(start, stop) starts at start and ends before stop. Print consecutive numbers starting at 1. Add 1, 2, and 3 one at a time. Which numbers does range(1, 3) produce? Print 2, 3, and 4 in order. Find the sum from 1 through 4. How many times does range(1, 1) run the loop body?

title: while loops and countdowns
subtitle: A while loop checks its condition before each iteration. True continues; false stops.
concept: A while loop checks its condition before each iteration. True continues; false stops.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python while loops and countdowns A while loop checks its condition before each iteration. True continues; false stops. A countdown takes another step while time remains and stops at 0. Check before each iteration while remaining > 0: runs its indented body only while remaining is positive. It tests the condition again on every iteration. A for loop is useful for going through items; a while loop is useful when a condition determines whether to continue. Move toward the stopping condition remaining = remaining - 1 reduces the value by 1. Starting at 3, it becomes 2, 1, then 0. At 0 the condition is false and the loop stops. Without that update, the condition stays true and the loop repeats indefinitely. Do not run the version with the update removed. Test small inputs and zero Count down from 3, then try 1, then 0. If the initial value is 0, the body never runs, but Done outside the loop still prints. Checking boundaries catches problems that a normal example can miss. A while loop checks first, runs its body only when the condition is true, then checks again after the body. Print 3, 2, 1, then Done. Start at 0. What prints if the countdown starts at 1? Count down from 2. Count from 0 through 2: print the current value, then add 1. With remaining equal to 0, how often does the body of while remaining > 0 run?

title: Errors and debugging
subtitle: When a program differs from your expectation, find the first wrong step and change one thing.
concept: When a program differs from your expectation, find the first wrong step and change one thing.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Errors and debugging When a program differs from your expectation, find the first wrong step and change one thing. Check a calculation by finding its first incorrect step, rather than looking only at the final answer. Write down the expected behavior To check the sum from 1 through 3, calculate 6 independently first. That is your expected result. If the program gives 3, avoid editing many lines at once. List the values number actually takes and find why 3 was omitted. Distinguish exceptions from wrong results An exception reports an error: a misspelled variable often causes NameError, and mixing a number with text often causes TypeError. Read the exception name on the last line, then follow the line number. A program that runs but gives 3 instead of 6 has a logic error: Python followed instructions that did not express your intention. Test nearby inputs after a fix range(1, 3) excludes 3; change it to range(1, 4). After the fix, test endpoints 1, 2, and 3. One successful example is not enough. Temporarily print(number) to inspect intermediate values, then remove the diagnostic print. Debug by stating an expectation, observing actual steps, and finding the earliest difference. Change one thing at a time. Fix the sum from 1 through 3. Print values to check each iteration. Fix nmae so the program prints the value of name. Fix the addition of the text "3" to the number 2. Add 1 through 2 and print each number being added. Test the fix with an endpoint of 0. What total do you expect?

title: Lists and shopping lists
subtitle: A list stores items in order. Read them by position or process them one by one.
concept: A list stores items in order. Read them by position or process them one by one.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Lists and shopping lists A list stores items in order. Read them by position or process them one by one. A shopping list has a first and second item, and you can add another at the end. Put items inside square brackets items = ["apple", "bread"] creates a list with two strings, separated by a comma inside square brackets. Lists preserve order. items[0] retrieves the first item; items[1] retrieves the second. Positions start at 0. len(items) gives the number of items, here 2. Append an item, then iterate items.append("milk") adds an item at the end. The dot selects an operation on this list; append is its name. for item in items: visits each item directly, without a range or an index. Two names can refer to one list other = items does not copy the list. It gives the same list another name, so appending through other also changes what items sees. For independent simple lists, use other = items.copy(). This is a shallow copy; here the list contains only strings or numbers. Lists preserve order and duplicates, and positions start at 0. append adds at the end; copy duplicates the simple, one-level lists used here. Read the first item, then print every item. Append an item and print the new length. What is the first item in [10, 20]? Append 30 to [10, 20], then print each item. Find the sum of [2, 3, 4]. Copy [1, 2] and append 3 only to the copy. How long is the original?

title: Dictionaries and key lookup
subtitle: A dictionary associates keys with values so you can look up a value by name.
concept: A dictionary associates keys with values so you can look up a value by name.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Dictionaries and key lookup A dictionary associates keys with values so you can look up a value by name. An address book finds a phone number by name, without needing its position. Write a price table prices = {"apple": 3, "bread": 5} is a dictionary. Each pair has a key on the left and its value on the right. A colon joins them; commas separate pairs. prices["apple"] retrieves 3 by key. These square brackets contain a key, not a list position. Add and update by key prices["milk"] = 4 adds a new product; prices["apple"] = 6 updates an existing price. Each key has one current value. for name in prices: visits the keys; prices[name] retrieves the corresponding value. Choose a default for a missing key Indexing a missing key raises KeyError. prices.get("rice", 0) retrieves the value if present and returns 0 otherwise, without inserting rice. This is useful for counting: counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1 starts an unseen item at 0 and adds one. A dictionary maps keys to values. Square brackets read an existing key; get can supply a default for a missing key. Look up apple, then change its price. Count occurrences in apple, pear, apple. Look up the bread price, 5. Update the bread price to 6. Return 0 for rice, which has no entry. Count fruits from an empty list. How many keys result?

title: Tuples and sets: records and distinct values
subtitle: Use a tuple for a fixed record and a set when you care which values occur.
concept: Use a tuple for a fixed record and a set when you care which values occur.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Tuples and sets: records and distinct values Use a tuple for a fixed record and a set when you care which values occur. A location is a pair of coordinates. A record of cities visited need not list the same city twice. Group a fixed pair of values point = (3, 4) creates a tuple using parentheses. As with a list, point[0] gives 3 and point[1] gives 4, but tuple positions cannot be reassigned. A tuple suits a fixed record such as coordinates. Here we use pairs; a one-item tuple needs a comma: (3,). Keep each distinct value once cities = {"Beijing", "Shanghai", "Beijing"} is a set. It keeps each distinct value once, so len(cities) is 2. With no colons, these are not dictionary key-value pairs. An empty set is set(); {} is an empty dictionary. Choose a container for the task "Beijing" in cities tests membership. A set has no first or second position and promises no display order. Use sorted(cities) for a consistently ordered list. Choose a list for order and duplicates, a dictionary for key-value lookup, a tuple for a fixed record, and a set for distinct values and membership. Tuple positions cannot be reassigned. A set keeps distinct values, and in tests membership. Retrieve both numbers from a coordinate pair. How many distinct cities are in Beijing, Shanghai, Beijing? What is the second item of (5, 8)? How many values remain after converting [1, 1, 2] to a set? Test whether 3 belongs to {1, 2}. Create an empty set and print its length.

title: Comprehensions and data processing
subtitle: A list comprehension is shorthand for processing items and collecting results. Understand the ordinary loop first.
concept: A list comprehension is shorthand for processing items and collecting results. Understand the ordinary loop first.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Comprehensions and data processing A list comprehension is shorthand for processing items and collecting results. Understand the ordinary loop first. Double each product's quantity and collect the results into a new list. Start with a familiar for loop Starting with values = [1, 2, 3], create result = []. In a loop, calculate value * 2 and add it with result.append(...). The result is [2, 4, 6]. The original remains [1, 2, 3] because the additions went into a new list. Express the same steps in one line result = [value * 2 for value in values] expresses the same simple process. Read the for clause first: take each value from values. Then read value * 2: what each item becomes. The surrounding brackets collect those results into a list. Add a filter when needed [value * 2 for value in values if value >= 2] keeps values at least 2, then doubles them, giving [4, 6]. Check a small list by hand. For nested loops or complicated conditions, an ordinary for loop may be clearer. The goal is to explain each result, not to minimize line count. [expression for item in data if condition] filters items, evaluates an expression, and collects the results in a new list. The condition is optional. Double 1, 2, and 3 separately. Keep values at least 2, then double them. Add 1 to each item in [1, 2] and collect a new list. Keep only values at least 2 from [1, 2, 3]. Solve the previous exercise with an ordinary loop. What results from doubling every item in an empty list?

title: Functions, parameters, and return values
subtitle: Name a reusable sequence of steps, give it input when calling it, and capture its result.
concept: Name a reusable sequence of steps, give it input when calling it, and capture its result.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Functions, parameters, and return values Name a reusable sequence of steps, give it input when calling it, and capture its result. A doubling machine takes 3 and returns 6. Give the steps a name def double(number): defines a function named double. A function is a reusable sequence of steps; number names its input and is called a parameter. The indented return number * 2 doubles it and sends the result to the caller. Defining the function records the steps; it does not yet compute with 3. Call the function and capture its result result = double(3) makes the call: number receives 3, the calculation produces 6, and return sends 6 back for result to hold. print(result) displays it. Call again with a different input without rewriting the function body. Returning and printing are different print displays content; return sends a value back to the caller. To continue calculating with the result, return it. A function that prints but has no return statement returns None, which cannot be used as a number in this calculation. Its parameter is local to the call. def defines a function; a call supplies input. return sends a result to the caller, while print displays content. Pass in 3, capture its double, and display it. Pass in 4 and add 1 to the returned result. Call the doubling function with 5. Write add_one to return its input plus 1. Call add_one twice, with 1 and then 4. What should the doubling function return for 0?

title: Arguments and default values
subtitle: Pass values by position or parameter name. Give a parameter a default for common cases.
concept: Pass values by position or parameter name. Give a parameter a default for common cases.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Arguments and default values Pass values by position or parameter name. Give a parameter a default for common cases. Order drinks by specifying price and quantity. If no quantity is given, prepare one. Identify what each input means def cost(price, count): has two parameters. cost(3, 2) passes 3 to price and 2 to count by position, producing 6. Reordering arguments can change their meaning. State the units of inputs such as unit price and quantity. Give a common value a default def cost(price, count=1): uses 1 when count is omitted. cost(3) buys one item; cost(3, 2) buys two. cost(price=3, count=2) uses keyword arguments to name the parameters explicitly. Here the defaulted parameter follows the required one. Decide whether a list input may change To total a list, read its items and return total without adding to or deleting from the input. This makes the function easier to predict. Start with numbers or strings as defaults: a default [] can be shared across calls. The optional note explains why. Arguments can be supplied by position or by name. A default applies when its argument is omitted. At unit price 3, buy one item and then two. Buy 3 items at unit price 4. Use unit price 5 and the default quantity 1. Call with unit price 5 and quantity 2 using parameter names. Write total_of to read [2, 3] and return its sum. What is the cost of quantity 0 at unit price 5?

title: Modules: reusable tools
subtitle: Put reusable functions in a separate file and import them from another file.
concept: Put reusable functions in a separate file and import them from another file.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Modules: reusable tools Put reusable functions in a separate file and import them from another file. Keep familiar tools in a toolbox and retrieve them by name. Use a built-in Python module import math loads Python's built-in math module, a collection of related tools. math.sqrt(9) calls its square-root function and returns 3.0. The dot joins the module name to the tool name. You do not need to implement the square-root algorithm. Put your tools in helpers.py The appendix defines double in helpers.py. After from helpers import double, main.py can call double(5). Save the files in one directory, enter it in a terminal, and run main.py. Do not name your own file math.py or json.py: it can hide the standard module. Keep demonstrations out of imports Ordinary top-level statements also execute the first time a module is imported. To avoid prompting the user during an import, put demonstrations and command-line operations under if __name__ == "__main__":. Treat this as an entry-point guard: it runs when the file is executed directly, not when imported. You need not study the double underscores yet. import makes module tools available. An entry-point guard runs a demonstration only when the file is executed directly. Find the square root of 9. Run this file directly to display the doubled value. Find the square root of 16. Find the square root of 0. Run an entry point that prints Tool demonstration. Import sqrt by itself and find the square root of 25.

title: Exceptions and input validation
subtitle: When users may enter invalid data, give a fallible conversion a clear failure path.
concept: When users may enter invalid data, give a fallible conversion a clear failure path.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Exceptions and input validation When users may enter invalid data, give a fallible conversion a clear failure path. Someone enters two instead of a numeric quantity. Explain the requirement before asking again. Find the operation that can fail int("3") succeeds, but int("three") raises ValueError: the text is unsuitable for this conversion. Without handling, the program stops there. Identify the error you intend to handle instead of wrapping everything in an indistinct failure case. Handle the expected failure with try and except The try body attempts the conversion. except ValueError: handles only that exception type. Success skips except; failure skips the remaining try statements and enters except. Handling an exception does not make the failed operation succeed: it provides understandable feedback. Conversion does not guarantee validity "-2" converts to an integer, but a shopping quantity cannot be negative. After conversion, test count < 0. A function can reject it with raise ValueError("Quantity cannot be negative"). Do not catch every exception indiscriminately, or spelling bugs and file problems may be misreported as quantity errors. try attempts a fallible operation; except handles a specified exception. raise explicitly rejects invalid input. Try converting three into a quantity. Define a quantity validator and test -2. Convert valid text "4" and display it. Handle the failure to convert "4.5" directly to an integer. Convert -1, then print Cannot be negative. Quantity 0 is allowed. What should the program display?

title: Text files and paths
subtitle: Variables disappear when a program ends. Save data to a file to read it next time.
concept: Variables disappear when a program ends. Save data to a file to read it next time.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Text files and paths Variables disappear when a program ends. Save data to a file to read it next time. Write today's list on paper so you can read it tomorrow. Choose where to write notes.txt is a filename. Without a full path, it is relative to the program's current working directory, which may differ from the code directory. Start in a separate practice folder. The web replay uses an isolated example directory and does not write files on your computer. Specify the file mode and text encoding with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file: opens a file for writing. Mode w truncates an existing file, so practice with a new filename. The encoding determines how text is stored; this book consistently uses UTF-8. file.write("Buy apples\n") writes text; \n is a newline. with closes the file when its indented block ends. Reading a file still gives text Open the same file in r mode. text = file.read() reads its contents as a string. Use print(text, end="") to preserve the file's newlines without adding another one. Mode a appends to existing content; check the destination first. with open(...) opens a file and closes it at the end of the block. r reads, w overwrites, and a appends. Write Buy apples, close the file, then read it again. Keep the first line and add a second with a. Write Hello to a new hello.txt, then read it. Append B to an example file containing A. Overwrite A with B using w in an example file. What is the length of the text read from an empty example file?

title: JSON and CSV: structures and tables
subtitle: JSON stores structures; CSV stores tables. After parsing, check both types and meaning.
concept: JSON stores structures; CSV stores tables. After parsing, check both types and meaning.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python JSON and CSV: structures and tables JSON stores structures; CSV stores tables. After parsing, check both types and meaning. Store a dictionary in a text file or organize a bill into table rows. Store a dictionary as JSON json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False) converts a dictionary to JSON text. Remember the s in dumps as string. ensure_ascii=False leaves non-ASCII characters readable. json.loads(text) converts the text back to data. This uses a standard data format rather than merely saving a dictionary's printed appearance. Read a small CSV table Each CSV row is a record, and the first row can name the columns. csv.DictReader reads each row as a dictionary using those names. Here io.StringIO wraps sample text as a file-like object; io provides input/output tools. You can also pass a real file opened with open to DictReader. A small text table separates table handling from path issues. Numeric CSV fields arrive as text An amount field may look like 125, but row["amount"] is the string "125". Convert it with int to integer cents before adding. A complete project also checks column names, missing values, and negative amounts. Successful parsing does not validate each row. Likewise, check that parsed JSON has the dictionary or list structure you need. JSON converts between structures and text; CSV reads column-based records. Validate structures and values after parsing. Convert a name and count to JSON, then read them back. The CSV amount column contains 125 and 200, in cents. Read count from JSON text. Convert [1, 2] to JSON and back, then print its length. Read a CSV amount of 50 and add 10. With only a CSV header and no data rows, what is the total?

title: Tests and boundary cases
subtitle: Specify inputs and correct results, then repeatedly compare them with the program's output.
concept: Specify inputs and correct results, then repeatedly compare them with the program's output.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Tests and boundary cases Specify inputs and correct results, then repeatedly compare them with the program's output. Give a machine small problems with known answers and check whether it keeps answering correctly. Calculate expectations independently For a doubling function, calculate expectations by hand: 3 gives 6, 0 gives 0, and -2 gives -4. Do not generate the expected answer by calling the function under test, or the same bug can appear on both sides. Tests preserve these checks so you can rerun them after changing the code. Write a check with assert assert double(3) == 6 requires the comparison to be true. == tests equality. Success continues silently; failure raises AssertionError. A final print("Checks passed") shows execution got through those assertions. Do not run these tests with Python's -O option: it disables assert statements. Cover ordinary and boundary cases Passing for 3 is not enough. Try 0, negative inputs, and values that expose likely bugs. Passing tests does not prove correctness for every input, but explicit boundary checks help prevent known bugs from returning. The project appendix uses unittest to run a suite. Start with input, expectation, and comparison. A test compares an actual result with an independently determined expectation. assert requires its condition to be true. Check an ordinary value, zero, and a negative value. Suppose doubling is mistakenly implemented as adding 2. Test input 3. Write a check for add_one(3). Write a boundary check for add_one(0). Check that the sum of an empty list is 0. Check that 3 candies in bags of 5 make 0 full bags with remainder 3.

title: Capstone: a local expense reporter
subtitle: Connect reading, validation, calculation, and display to build an expense summary tool.
concept: Connect reading, validation, calculation, and display to build an expense summary tool.
text: Introduction to Python Programming Introduction to Programming with Python python Capstone: a local expense reporter Connect reading, validation, calculation, and display to build an expense summary tool. Read the bill, validate amounts, total them by category, then display a report. Start with a bill you can check by hand Take food at 125 cents, transport at 200, and food at 75. Calculate independently: food totals 200, transport 200, and the grand total is 400 cents. Start with three in-memory records, combining Chapter 3 lists and dictionaries with Chapter 4 functions. Do not add files, command-line parsing, and tests all at once. Separate four responsibilities First read CSV (Section 5.2). Second validate columns, category, and integer-cent amounts, rejecting zero and negatives (Section 4.4). Third accumulate amounts by category in a dictionary (Section 3.2). Fourth display results in a stable order. Verify the accumulation before connecting file input. The appendix provides complete source with a function for each responsibility. Add the command-line interface last Save the appendix source and sample.csv in one folder and enter it in a terminal. Run python3 expense_report.py --help to check usage, then python3 expense_report.py sample.csv. Store amounts as integer cents and convert to currency units only for display. A CLI accepts arguments through terminal commands; argparse reads the filename. The class declarations in the full tests organize unittest cases; object-oriented mechanisms belong in a later course. The reporter separates reading, validation, aggregation, and display. Each record must contain a positive integer amount in cents. Sum three small records by category. Assume the records have already been validated and contain positive integer cents. Display 375 cents as 3.75 currency units. Two amounts in the same category are 100 and 50 cents. What is their total? Display 150 cents as currency units with two decimal places. Check amounts 0 and -1 cents. This project requires each amount to be positive. With no records, what is the total in cents?

title: Start with a real problem
subtitle: Replace an impressive-sounding product idea with an observable situation.
